62-076.r: Marasmus → prolonged starvation; Kwashiorkor → protein deficiency; T.B. → bacterial infection; Hepatitis B → viral infection.

62-077.r: Kwashiorkor → acute malnutrition from protein deficiency in diet; swelling, enlarged liver; usually infants and children up to about 5 years.

62-078.r: Marasmus → disease of children from prolonged starvation: general wasting of the body due to both energy and protein deficiency.
62-078.t: Marasmus = energy + protein lack (wasting); Kwashiorkor = mainly protein lack (swelling).

62-079.r: Jaundice → liver. Cataract → eye; Typhoid → intestine; Pneumonia → lungs.

62-080.r: Pneumonia → lungs. Cataract → eye; Jaundice → liver; Diabetes → metabolism.

62-081.r: Astigmatism → eye defect: cornea or lens not perfectly curved → blurred or distorted vision; a refractive error (like myopia, hypermetropia).

62-082.r: Myopia (near-sightedness) → eye disorder: light focuses in front of the retina, so distant objects look blurry.

62-083.r: Myopia (short-sightedness) → corrected with a concave lens; image of far object forms in front of the retina.
62-083.h: Myopia → Minus (concave) lens; Hypermetropia → Plus (convex) lens.

62-084.r: Myopia → nearby objects seen clearly, distant objects blurred; corrected by concave (divergent) lens.

62-085.r: Far-sightedness (hypermetropia) → near objects blurred, image forms beyond retina (short eyeball or flat lens); corrected by convex (convergent) lens.

62-086.r: Blind spot (optic disc, no visual cells, where optic nerve leaves) and yellow spot (macula lutea, image formation) → both in the retina.

62-087.r: Retina → develops as an outgrowth of the brain's diencephalon (optic stalk becomes optic nerve; optic vesicle → optic cup).

62-088.r: Cataract → eye lens becomes opaque (mostly in older people); treated by removing the lens, intraocular lens implant, or laser.

62-090.r: Cataract → lens turns cloudy because its proteins break down and clump together (around age 40 and above).

62-091.r: Atropine → dilation of pupil; Ether → local anaesthesia; Nitroglycerine → heart trouble (vasodilator for angina); Pyrethrin → mosquito control.

62-092.r: Atropine (alkaloid from belladonna plants) → very dilute solution dilates the pupil during eye examinations.

62-093.r: Ishihara test → colour blindness (red-green deficiency); by Shinobu Ishihara, Tokyo, 1917; 38 pseudoisochromatic plates.

62-094.r: Biological resurfacing → knee (cultured cartilage cells re-inserted), hip (alternative to Total Hip Replacement), ankle and vertebral joints. The book gives no single answer (*).

62-095.r: Iron deficiency → anaemia (too few healthy red blood cells); iron is the main part of haemoglobin; body needs about 12 mg iron a day.

62-097.r: Excessive alcohol → liver cirrhosis (normal liver tissue replaced by scar tissue, fibrosis).

62-098.r: Oral submucous fibrosis → premalignant mouth disease from chewing betel quid or areca nut; gutka (tobacco) is a manufactured betel quid.

62-099.r: Jaundice → affects the liver; high blood bilirubin gives yellow skin and eyes (seen in hepatitis, liver cancer).

62-100.r: Jaundice → not contagious (book); measles, cholera, T.B. are contagious. In jaundice skin and eyes turn yellowish.

62-101.r: Rickets (also in poultry/chickens) → vitamin D deficiency (or lack of phosphorus, calcium): poor bone calcification, fractures, deformity.

62-102.r: Mad cow disease → caused by prions (distorted protein) in the brain of cattle; not bacteria, virus or fungus.

62-103.r: Liver fluke → endoparasite in bile ducts of sheep ('sheep liver fluke'); mammal is primary host, snail is intermediate host.

62-104.r: Bright's disease (nephritis) → kidney disorder; kidney blood vessels inflamed, albumin passes in urine.

62-105.r: Pneumoconiosis → occupational lung disease from inhaling dust, mainly in coal mining workers.

62-106.r: Blood glucose → milligram per decilitre (or mmol/L); normal about 82 to 110 mg/dL (4.4 to 6.1 mmol/L); after a meal up to 140 mg/dL.

62-107.r: Overdose injection (insulin) → spasm, apoplexy, faintness, death due to abnormal blood glucose; insulin regulates blood sugar.

62-108.r: Diabetes → no vaccine (insulin shortage from pancreas); polio, whooping cough, smallpox are controlled by vaccination.

62-109.r: Diabetes → linked to pancreas: too little insulin (made by beta cells of islets of Langerhans) or body cannot use it → high blood glucose.

62-111.r: Lack of insulin (pancreatic hormone) → diabetes; patients pass excess urine (polyuria).

62-112.r: Diabetes mellitus → higher sugar in blood + lower insulin in blood (statements 1 and 3).

62-113.r: Glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) test → management of diabetes mellitus; shows average blood glucose of previous 8 to 12 weeks.

62-114.r: Diabetes insipidus → large urine output, thirst (A true); caused by LACK of ADH (vasopressin), not excess (R false).
62-114.t: Insipidus = ADH problem; mellitus = insulin problem.

62-115.r: Whiskey increases urination (A true) because alcohol SUPPRESSES vasopressin (ADH), not speeds it up (R false).

62-116.r: Fenugreek seeds → lower blood sugar in diabetes (slow sugar absorption, stimulate insulin).

62-117.r: Curry leaf tree (native of India) → claimed cure for diabetes (British researchers; multi-billion dollar potential).

62-118.r: Insulin → discovered by Canadian F.G. Banting with Best (help of Macleod); Banting and Macleod got the Nobel Prize, 1923.

62-119.r: Copper-T (Cu-T) contraceptive → commonest side effect: more bleeding during the menstrual cycle.

62-120.r: Emphysema → lung disease (a form of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, COPD) linked to environmental pollution.

62-121.r: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) → non-narcotic analgesic (so 'narcotic' is false); relieves pain, fever, inflammation; prevents blood clots.
62-121.t: Aspirin is NON-narcotic; morphine-type drugs are narcotic.

62-122.r: CPR = Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation → emergency chest compressions plus artificial breathing when breathing or heartbeat stops.

62-123.r: Coronary artery bypass graft → any of: vein from the leg, artery from forearm/wrist, or artery from chest (mammary region).

62-124.r: Cath lab (catheterisation laboratory) → in cardiology department; imaging of heart arteries and chambers, treats stenosis.

62-125.r: Top-priority nutritional deficiency in India → xerophthalmia (severe vitamin A lack; dry, keratinised conjunctiva and cornea).

62-126.r: Lathyrism → excess khesari dal (Lathyrus sativus): neurological disorder with weakness, spasms, paralysis of lower limbs.

62-128.r: Blank capsules → mainly gelatine (melts in stomach), also starch; book gives both (c) and (d).
